To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IFN-γ produced during T cell-mediated immunity to influenza virus in the lungs of mice inhibits initial pulmonary phagocytic defense against bacteria, leading to enhanced susceptibility to subsequent pneumococcal pneumonia, which can be blocked by IFN-β treatment or by anti-IFN-γ antibodies.
IFN-γ produced during T cell-mediated responses to influenza infection inhibits the ability of alveolar macro phages to clear bacterial pathogens from the lung.

IFN-γ produced during influenza infection in mice can inhibit pulmonary antibacterial defense and that this inhibition is mediated by downregulation of the expression of the macrophage receptor MARCO.

understanding how the immune system protects the lung against bacterial infection and how this defense is compromised during influenza virus infection.
